title: Kenyan Garlic Sauce
community: Popular in urban Kenya — restaurant and home favourite
author: Mama Wanjiru
desc: Kenyan Garlic Sauce — a thick, creamy, intensely garlicky white sauce made from roasted garlic, lemon, and natural yogurt or mayonnaise. The addictive dipping sauce for chips, grilled chicken, and mishkaki that has become a Kenyan restaurant staple.
longDesc: Kenyan garlic sauce is the condiment that regular customers know to ask for at their favourite restaurants — a thick, creamy, pungent white sauce that transforms chips, grilled chicken, and mishkaki into something extraordinary. It sits between a garlic aioli and a yogurt-based dip, with a distinctly Kenyan character from the lemon and fresh coriander.
ingredients: 1 cup natural yogurt or mayonnaise (or half each)
steps: For roasted garlic: wrap unpeeled cloves in foil and roast at 180°C for 20 minutes until soft and golden. Squeeze out roasted garlic.
For raw garlic version: mince garlic very finely or crush in a mortar.
Combine garlic, yogurt/mayonnaise, lemon juice, coriander, salt, pepper, and olive oil.
Blend until smooth or mix thoroughly by hand for a more textured result.
Taste and adjust salt and lemon.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes before serving — the flavour develops.
chefTips: Roasted garlic gives a sweeter, more mellow sauce — raw garlic is sharper and more pungent. Both are delicious.
A combination of yogurt and mayonnaise gives the best texture — yogurt alone is too thin.
Resting in the refrigerator for 30 minutes is important — the flavour deepens significantly.
commonMistakes: Too much lemon — can curdle the yogurt.
Not resting before serving — the flavour is flat when just made.
cookingScience: Roasting garlic converts its harsh, pungent allicin into sweeter, milder ajoene and vinyldithiin compounds. This is why roasted garlic sauce has a completely different flavour profile from raw garlic sauce — less sharp, more rounded, and more aromatic.
sustainabilityTips: Roast garlic in the oven while cooking other dishes to save energy.
healthBenefits: Garlic provides allicin — antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory.
culturalNote: Kenyan garlic sauce has become a restaurant institution — the white sauce that regular customers specifically request. Its popularity reflects Kenya's enthusiastic embrace of bold, flavourful condiments.
